notes: Both entries are REAL, OPEN defects of the same class as R-LX-24, not accepted behaviour. They are carried
rather than fixed because the fix belongs on PRODUCTION as well as here: 20260912_lx4_channel_listing_translations
and 20260912_lx5_readiness_index both end with a GRANT and neither enables row-level security or creates the
nexus_workspace_isolation policy, and both folders are already applied on production (commit da1078ddf). The gate
prints every carried entry on every run for that reason. The SQL is in CLOSE.1's ledger section; the Owner decides
the predicate (the simple workspace clause or the fuller one 20260911_category_taxonomies uses), which is the same
open question R-LX-24 already put in front of them.
CLOSE.1 applied no DDL: the local database is shared with a running API on :8091 and two lanes in flight, and a
local-only fix would have turned this gate green while production kept the gap.
violations: ChannelListingTranslation: row-level security is NOT enabled, and the table carries workspaceId — a routed read returns every workspace's rows
ReadinessIndex: row-level security is NOT enabled, and the table carries workspaceId — a routed read returns every workspace's rows
